**1 — Scene:** I’m treating the **central chicken-and-shredded-vegetable salad** as the meal. The sandwiches, sushi, fruit, cookie and drinks are on separate vessels and excluded.

**2 — Vessel:** A shallow plate approximately **24 cm in diameter**. Area = 3.14 × 12² ≈ **452 cm²**.

**3 — Items:** Sliced cooked chicken, shredded cabbage, leafy greens, tomato and a little shredded carrot. No separate oil or dressing is clearly identifiable, so none is added.

**4–7 — Area, volume, weight and energy:** Footprint percentages partition the salad’s visible coverage; heights represent each component’s average pile thickness.

| Item | Vessel area | Gross volume: area × height | Density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Cooked chicken | 25% = 113 cm² | 113 × 1.1 = 124 ml | 0.95 | 118 g | 165 | 195 kcal |
| Shredded cabbage | 20% = 90 cm² | 90 × 1.5 = 135 ml | 0.60 | 81 g | 25 | 20 kcal |
| Leafy greens | 20% = 90 cm² | 90 × 2 = 180 ml | 0.15 | 27 g | 20 | 5 kcal |
| Tomato | 3% = 14 cm² | 14 × 1.2 = 17 ml | 0.60 | 10 g | 18 | 2 kcal |
| Shredded carrot | 2% = 9 cm² | 9 × 0.7 = 6 ml | 0.60 | 4 g | 41 | 2 kcal |

**8 — Sanity check:** Food covers approximately **70%** of the plate. About **240 g and 224 kcal** is plausible for this shallow salad, with roughly half its weight coming from chicken. Any unidentifiable dressing would increase the energy estimate.
